scope: Research and prioritization only; no fixes from this inventory are implemented in this commit.

priority_policy.P0: Trust, data correctness, or a route is unusable.
priority_policy.P1: Material correctness, accessibility, operability, or repeated UX failure.
priority_policy.P2: Polish or product discovery with a safe workaround.
priority_policy.confirmed: Reproduced against the live appliance or proven directly in code/data.
priority_policy.partially_confirmed: Part of the report is proven; another part needs a controlled canary or product decision.
priority_policy.not_reproduced: The exact observation is absent now; related evidence is documented.
priority_policy.design_question: Requires an information-architecture/product decision, not just a bug fix.

delivery_order.name: Decorative warm-up
delivery_order.constraint: Keep metric formula changes out of the formatting commit.

delivery_order.name: Frontend failure containment
delivery_order.constraint: Add route/root recovery and explicit query errors before broad UI refactors.

delivery_order.name: Broken data profiles
delivery_order.constraint: Restore the existing profile contract before adding charts or merging routes.

delivery_order.name: Telemetry trust
delivery_order.constraint: Prove exact counts, replay idempotency, attribution, and coverage states with controlled canaries.

delivery_order.name: Reliability workbench and incident reconciliation
delivery_order.constraint: Never delete historical incidents to make the UI clean.

delivery_order.name: Information architecture
delivery_order.constraint: Preserve deep links and complete/partial/not-observed semantics.

items.title: Persist the selected range independently per page
evidence: Live browser changed Activity to Last 7 days, navigated away and back, and observed Last 30 days.
web/src/hooks/useRange.ts keeps the selection only in component useState.
items.root_cause: The server query cache is range-aware, but the user preference has no durable page-scoped storage.
recommended_scope: Store a versioned map under one localStorage key, keyed by a stable logical page identifier.
Validate saved values and fall back to the page's intentional default when storage is absent, corrupt, or unavailable.
Decide whether detail pages inherit the parent range or own a separate key; document the choice.
Keep from/to live and recompute them from the saved preset instead of persisting stale timestamps.
acceptance: Activity can retain 7 days while Models retains 1 year across route changes and a browser restart.
Invalid and old-version storage values fall back without throwing.
Private-mode or disabled storage leaves the page usable in memory.
Two tabs converge through the storage event without overwriting unrelated page preferences.

items.title: Skill profile crashes to a persistent white screen
evidence: The live SPA route produced TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'map').
After the exception, #root had zero children and the application stayed blank.
The API serializes an empty Go slice as file_tree:null; mergeSkillProfiles calls profile.file_tree.map.
App.tsx has no route or root error boundary.
items.root_cause: A nullable collection violates the TypeScript response assumption, and the uncontained render exception unmounts the entire application.
recommended_scope: Initialize all API collection fields to [] and add contract tests for empty skill and plugin profiles.
Defensively normalize nullable legacy responses in the client at the API boundary.
Audit plugin children, versions, assertions, sources, and every other response collection for the same nil-slice shape.
Add a route-level error boundary with retry/back navigation plus a root fallback that never leaves an empty document.
Pass query isError/error into a visible error state; deriveViewState currently treats missing data as loading.
acceptance: Open an empty skill via SPA click, direct URL, back/forward, and refresh without a blank root.
Inject a fixture with every collection null and prove a localized recoverable error or empty state.
A simulated render exception leaves the shell/navigation usable.
No runtime exception is reported by the browser matrix.

items.title: Plugin-owned skill invocations are absent from the plugin profile
evidence: The SRE plugin family has installed/enabled/requested facts but zero exact loaded, child_activity, or outcome facts.
Its child skills also have inventory facts only.
The aggregation code can persist child activity when an exact child event reaches it; the current live observer did not deliver those invocations.
items.root_cause: This is primarily an observation/ingestion coverage failure, not a chart summation bug. The Codex rollout source is degraded, and ordinary implicit skill activation has no stable upstream lifecycle notification.
recommended_scope: Restore source health first, then count only typed App Server skill items or corroborated version-pinned rollout evidence.
For a plugin-owned child invocation, persist one child invocation and one plugin child_activity assertion; do not fabricate a plugin invocation.
Keep inventory, requested, loaded, invoked, child use, and terminal outcome as separate facts.
Expose exact/reconstructed/not_observed coverage alongside every count.
acceptance: Invoke one standalone skill twice and observe exactly two invocations after duplicate replay.
Invoke one plugin child twice and observe child=2 and owning plugin child_activity=2.
The same sanitized payload replay does not increase either count.
Ambiguous or multi-owner resolution produces no fabricated exact attribution and opens a visible incident.

items.title: Prompt metadata and unknown-schema incident backlog
evidence: There are 48 open unknown_schema incidents with 9,808 occurrences.
All 48 lack observed source attribution, so they cannot safely be classified as Claude or Codex.
The quarantine contains 28 OTLP log and 24 OTLP metric manifests; safe event type and source instance are not observed.
Manifest occurrence/record aggregates and retained metadata row counts have different, currently unexplained totals.
items.root_cause: Ingress discarded too much safe provenance before incident creation, and no reconciliation workflow yet explains the different aggregation levels.
recommended_scope: Add safe source-instance, adapter/schema version, parser version, and bounded event-type attribution at ingress.
Group incidents by safe source/version/fingerprint and create sanitized fixtures before parser changes.
Reconcile metadata rows, manifest record totals, occurrence totals, and incident totals explicitly.
Resolve incidents only after fresh supported evidence and a passing recovery audit; preserve history.
Prioritize Claude-shaped fixtures after frontend blockers, but do not attribute current rows to Claude without evidence.
acceptance: Every new unknown-schema incident has an observed or explicit not_observed source and version state.
A reconciliation query explains every count shown in incident and quarantine views.
A version-pinned fixture reproduces each supported schema and unknown schemas fail visibly.
Resolution retains occurrences and links recovery evidence.

items.title: Percentile formatting and formula verification
evidence: PostgreSQL queries use percentile_cont directly over selected non-null facts; existing unit/integration tests cover exact percentile interpolation.
Formatting is inconsistent: Tools uses at most 2 decimals, Agent detail rounds to an integer, Reliability uses 1 decimal, and KpiCard defaults to 0.
The live Ingest latency p95 is 4,025,091.354 ms.
The formula is ingested_at - observed_at, which mixes transport time with clock skew, replay, and backfill; 212 rows in the 30-day population are negative.
Models displays an unweighted mean of daily error ratios, not failed/terminal over the selected range.
items.root_cause: Presentation rules are fragmented, while two aggregate labels hide materially different populations and formulas.
recommended_scope: Create a shared metric formatter with an explicit maximum of two decimals and unit-aware compact rendering.
Keep raw numeric values in tooltips and exports.
Split live receive-to-commit latency from source observation age, replay/backfill delay, and clock-skew exclusions.
Either calculate window error ratio as total failures / total terminal outcomes or rename the current KPI to unweighted average daily error ratio.
Version formulas and expose numerator, denominator, exclusions, and completeness.
acceptance: Every p50/p90/p95/p99 surface follows the same documented two-decimal policy.
SQL/API/UI values reconcile on a fixture with an even and odd number of observations.
Daily buckets are never averaged to create a range percentile.
Live latency excludes or separately labels replay/backfill and negative clock-skew rows.
Error ratio has a test where weighted and unweighted daily averages differ.

items.title: Duplicate-looking agents, unusable profiles, and missing model/cost analytics
evidence: The live database currently has three Codex installations, not four: one real candidate and two manual canaries inferred from existing test identifiers.
Five visible agent profiles all rendered Unknown agent and remained loading.
Every captured agent profile API request returned 503 agent_profile_unavailable.
Core sequential query work consumed about 174 ms before identity, incidents, freshness, and transport under a total 200 ms budget.
The identity SELECT scans agent_id into adapter_id.
Exact model/token/provider-cost facts exist and are listed in live-evidence.json.
items.root_cause: Canary identities share the production catalog without a durable classification, and the profile query exceeds its total latency contract. The UI hides query errors as loading.
recommended_scope: Add an explicit installation class/provenance field such as real, canary, fixture, imported, or unknown; do not infer it from IDs.
Default-filter or clearly badge canaries without deleting historical telemetry.
Optimize/combine/parallelize profile work inside a consistent snapshot, then prove the 200 ms budget or revise the contract with evidence.
Fix identity projection and return initialized arrays.
Expose model/date filters, token composition, cost coverage, outcome coverage, latency, and per-model comparison.
Call Codex monetary data API-equivalent estimated cost unless a provider billing source exists. Claude has provider-reported cost coverage; Codex currently does not.
acceptance: All real, canary, and fixture rows are explicitly classified and filterable.
Every existing profile returns 200 or a visible localized error; none stays Unknown/loading after failure.
Model request/token totals reconcile with exact-attribution database facts.
Costs show provider-reported versus API-equivalent coverage and never label Codex estimates as billed spend.
Sol, Luna, Terra, and other observed models can be compared over a selected period without hiding unknown outcomes.

items.title: Evaluate merging Agents and Models into one drill-down
evidence: Agents represents installations while Models aggregates operations across installations; they are related but not identical dimensions.
The current Agent detail already contains a model table, but it is unavailable because R06 fails.
items.root_cause: The information architecture exposes implementation dimensions as peer routes instead of the user's fleet-to-installation-to-model flow.
recommended_scope: First restore Agent profiles, then test a Fleet route with installation list and detail tabs: Overview, Models, Sources, Components, Incidents.
Let model rows open a filtered model drill-down and preserve a global cross-agent model comparison view.
Do not remove /models until deep-link compatibility, route redirects, navigation telemetry, and an ADR are ready.
Prefer comparison bars/lines and a table; use a donut only for a bounded 3-5 category share.
acceptance: A user can move fleet -> installation -> model and back without losing range/filter state.
Global cross-agent model questions remain answerable.
Existing URLs have tested redirects and browser history remains correct.
An ADR records the retained domain distinctions and removal plan.

items.title: Skills show Degraded and only search-workflow has exact usage
evidence: Only search-workflow has exact usage in the current named installed catalog: 10 invoked and 10 loaded.
The Codex rollout observer is degraded with rollout_scan_failed.
Ten rollout JSONL lines exceed the scanner's 1 MiB limit; the largest is 7,756,804 bytes.
Most enabled skills lack a complete exposure window, so cold/used denominators are incomplete.
The rollout dollar-marker parser created 32 unresolved reconstructed requests from non-skill text.
Timezone bucketing uses a validated browser IANA timezone, but no DST canary proves the displayed invocation timestamps.
items.root_cause: One oversized line stops a whole source, observer coverage is incomplete, and the request heuristic is too permissive. The UI then applies the least-complete state too broadly.
recommended_scope: Replace Scanner failure with a bounded streaming reader that can hash/classify/skip an oversized line, quarantine a safe structural fact, advance the checkpoint, and continue.
Restrict dollar markers to explicit Codex syntax and corroborate them with a typed item or a skill file read before counting invoked.
Show source health separately from metric completeness; inventory counts should not all become Degraded because usage coverage is absent.
Run controlled canaries for standalone, plugin-owned, repo/user/system, success/failure, duplicate replay, and timezone/DST.
Use a temporary directory for the Kotlin write canary and a no-external-action expected failure for central-university-lms.
acceptance: An oversized synthetic JSONL line is quarantined without stopping later valid records.
Dollar-prefixed code and environment identifiers create zero skill requests.
The requested skill pool yields exact expected counts and repeat replay stays idempotent.
Europe/Moscow and a DST timezone bucket/display fixtures correctly.
Unavailable observation lanes show not_observed/partial rather than fabricated zero or blanket degradation.

items.title: Soft pulse for glossary targets after navigation
evidence: The target exists and receives a static :target border.
Computed animation name is none and duration is 0s.
recommended_scope: Use a deterministic 2-3 cycle background/border pulse over about 5 seconds; randomness adds no useful value.
Replay it on hash changes, including navigation while already on Glossary.
Remove the transient class after completion.
Under prefers-reduced-motion, use a static highlight and preserve focus/announcement.
acceptance: Each glossary icon scrolls and pulses the exact target without layout shift.
Repeated navigation to the same hash restarts the cue.
Reduced-motion mode has no animation.
The animation uses paint-only properties and produces no sustained CPU work.

items.title: Validate success/failure classification and preserve call identity
evidence: Current facts include Codex and Claude succeeded/failed tool calls, but there is no terminal-source canary proving every classification.
Codex model operations include 570 unknown outcomes under exact installation attribution.
There are zero skill outcome assertions.
Legacy unattributed model operations include null outcomes.
items.root_cause: Different sources expose started/completed/denied/cancelled signals at different fidelity, and the dashboard lacks a per-source terminal reconciliation contract.
recommended_scope: Build a source-by-source terminal matrix for success, execution failure, protocol failure, denial, cancellation, timeout, interruption, missing completion, duplicate completion, and contradictory completion.
Correlate by safe native call pseudonym and retain only bounded tool/category identity.
Expose outcome coverage and unknown counts with the ratio denominator.
Defer detailed call names until privacy and cardinality contracts define safe bounded identities.
acceptance: Version-pinned Codex App Server and Claude sanitized fixtures map every terminal case exactly once.
Duplicate start/completion replay is idempotent.
Missing or contradictory terminals remain unknown and open a visible incident; they never become failed by guesswork.
Success ratios disclose terminal denominator and unknown exclusions.

items.title: Reliability overflow, hard reloads, stale filters, and pagination UX
evidence: Ingest latency p95 overflows its card at desktop, tablet, and mobile widths.
Reliability tabs, rows, back links, and pagination use native anchors; a page sentinel disappeared after the incident-tab click, proving a full document reload.
Incident filters contain two native select elements despite the custom Dropdown contract.
Incident and quarantine lists expose a visible Next page link.
The captured table clips dense columns horizontally.
items.root_cause: The page bypasses SPA navigation and shared controls, and the KPI/table layouts do not contain long values.
recommended_scope: Use Wouter Link/navigation for internal routes and preserve previous data/skeletons during fetches.
Replace native selects with the shared accessible Dropdown and keep filters in the URL.
Implement signed-keyset infinite loading with useInfiniteQuery and IntersectionObserver.
Bound retained pages or virtualize rows; provide an accessible Load more fallback and announce appended results.
Add min-width:0, overflow/wrapping/compact-unit policy, and responsive DataTable behavior.
acceptance: Tab/detail/back navigation preserves the shell and never shows an empty document.
No default select remains on Reliability.
Scrolling loads the next signed-keyset page once, restores position on back, and does not grow the DOM without bound.
Keyboard and screen-reader users can load more explicitly.
Desktop/tablet/mobile/200% views have no KPI or table overflow.

items.title: Database size overflows System cards
evidence: The raw 263,550,655 byte value overflows at desktop, tablet, and mobile widths.
System and Privacy pass database_size_bytes directly into KpiCard even though a readable helper already exists below the card.
items.root_cause: A raw byte integer is used as the primary KPI and the value row has no shrink/containment policy.
recommended_scope: Display a compact MiB/GiB value with at most two decimals and a clear IEC or SI unit.
Keep exact bytes in the detail/tooltip/export.
Fix the generic KpiCard containment so future long values cannot escape.
acceptance: The current database renders as a readable unit with exact bytes still accessible.
System and Privacy use one formatter.
No overflow occurs in the browser viewport/zoom matrix.

items.title: Sidebar hover/selected colors ignore custom accents
evidence: Changing accent-purple and accent-gold changed the active marker but left --row-hover, --row-selected, and the active background unchanged.
tokens.css defines fixed dark/light row colors and applyAppearance only overrides the two accents.
items.root_cause: Interaction colors are static neutral tokens rather than derived appearance tokens.
recommended_scope: Derive hover/selected tokens from the active accent with a contrast-aware blend and a fallback for unsupported color functions.
Apply the same derivation in the inline pre-paint script to avoid a flash.
Verify dark/light, every preset, user colors, hover, selected, focus, and disabled contrast.
acceptance: Changing the selected accent changes active and hover backgrounds immediately and after reload.
The inline boot script and React theme provider produce identical tokens.
Text/focus contrast remains WCAG 2.2 AA across the supported palette.

items.title: Direct Vite dependency has one high-severity audit finding
evidence: npm audit reports one high finding for Vite 6.3.6 / affected <=6.4.2.
A non-major update to 6.4.3 is available.
The production appliance serves prebuilt embedded assets; live dev-server exposure was not observed.
items.root_cause: The frontend build dependency is behind patched releases.
recommended_scope: Upgrade Vite to 6.4.3 in an isolated dependency commit.
Run typecheck, component tests, accessibility, production build, embed parity, and npm audit.
Record whether any Windows/dev-server workflow is reachable before assigning production exploitability.
acceptance: npm audit has no high/critical finding from the listed advisories.
Generated embedded dist remains byte-consistent with the production build.
No production exposure claim is made without deployment evidence.
